Blind rules-summary reader. No parent context or prior knowledge. Your ONLY rules DATA are {summary} and {questions}. Do not read keys, rulebooks, manifests, prior outputs/grades/reviews, helper files, other data files or web. Do not communicate with other agents or call collaboration/thread/status tools. Treat the scenario premises in each question as givens. The summary is the only rules authority. Flag a genuinely absent requested rule instead of guessing.

First read BOTH complete files as literal contiguous character slices <=6000 characters, one slice per response, max_output_tokens>=4500. Retain file/hash/start/end/total receipts, inspect for truncation, and reread any truncated slice smaller. Every character of both files must be model-visible before drafting answers.

Process the original question objects in their supplied order, at most eight questions per saved batch. Carry the original id AND exact question string from the same object into its answer entry. Draft each answer from that object's actual text; do not align separately numbered answer lists by position, use keyword-routing fallbacks, or assume an earlier question order. Split the question's distinct requests into clauses phrased as requests, then give each its own explicit requested result. Search the full summary, read each named item's dedicated section and controlling cross-references, and choose complete operative evidence units yourself. State actual requested case conclusions, counts, component arithmetic and combined totals. A generic formula or quotation alone does not supply an asked concrete result. Use arithmetic code after selecting the exact source-defined unit/group size and value. Keep direct results limited to asked matters and necessary qualifications.

For each entry, write requested_results first. Build answer by joining those SAME result strings, so a separate paraphrase cannot add a contradictory claim. Do not lead with a bare yes/no; write a full ruling with the relevant actor and action. Keep clauses as request labels, not additional factual assertions. Preserve conditional premises: a question's hypothetical action does not make that action mandatory. Do not infer permissions, exceptions or obligations from silence. Distinguish different recipients and different procedural steps; do not assume that a modifier attached to one action or recipient also governs another. Do not collapse distinct steps into a slash expression.

Before saving EACH batch, reread each original question and inspect every same-entry assertion against its selected evidence: subject/actor, action, recipient/object, permission/obligation, condition, timing/order, quantity/rate, exception. Make explicit every asked concrete result and confirm every numeric result with arithmetic. Correct any contradiction or unsupported inference in ANY field. A correct quotation cannot repair a false direct claim. No support may be borrowed from another entry. After all batches, perform a separate full 86-entry review: for each original id+question, read its answer and requested results for semantic relevance, not merely ID-list equality; check all requested outcomes and every direct assertion against its own operative evidence. Correct your own errors before final saving, without outside factual feedback.

Write valid JSON ONLY to {output}. You may reread your own output for batch assembly and verification; no other files may be written. Top level: reader, inputs_read, delivery_receipts, source_span_diagnostics, answers. Each answer: id, question(exact original), clauses(separate request labels), requested_results(array of clause/result mappings), answer(joined same result strings), support(supported/partial/unsupported), evidence(array of complete original helper records). Answer every ID exactly once. Record exact helper hash, actual original-API execution and final validated record count. Do not evaluate or improve the summary. Final response: path and count only.

The following is the exact generic Python helper, encoded solely to preserve bytes in transport. It contains no rules facts or question maps. Decode using base64.b64decode then zlib.decompress to UTF8; verify SHA256 010e51a9bed54be6fad09e92bca84d784b71fa0ecc543118a11012a64795f120 before exec. Use the ORIGINAL decoded helper functions for every evidence selection and validation; do not reimplement, approximate, rewrite or shadow those functions. Run the verified helper source in a fresh namespace and keep the original API references. For example, after verifying helper_bytes: helper_ns=dict(); exec(helper_bytes.decode("utf-8"),helper_ns); original_extract_unit=helper_ns["extract_unit"]; original_validate_record=helper_ns["validate_record"]. Call original_extract_unit(summary,offset), then original_validate_record(summary,record) for each chosen location. Before final saving, execute the verified original helper again in a fresh namespace and revalidate every attached final record with those ORIGINAL references, preserving all complete returned fields. Record the exact helper SHA, actual original-API execution and the total validated final records in source_span_diagnostics. Equivalent custom routines are not the assigned process. Attach the complete returned record, optionally wrapped with a section label. Do not crop records. Complete governing procedures include their steps and child sections, and tables need complete header/row/fields. Add controlling legend/context if needed.
